User Impact: 0

Synopsis

A hosting-provider compromise let attackers selectively redirect Notepad++ update traffic in 2025. Victims received malicious update.exe chains that led to Cobalt Strike and custom backdoors.

Story

Notepad++ disclosed the incident on 2026-02-02, but the attack window sat in 2025. The project's update infrastructure was affected by a hosting provider-level compromise that let attackers redirect selected update requests.

Kaspersky telemetry showed rotating chains from late July through October 2025. The legitimate updater process `GUP.exe` launched attacker-supplied `update.exe` files, which gathered host data, staged files under user profile directories, and delivered second-stage payloads.

The payloads changed over time. Some chains led to Cobalt Strike Beacon through Metasploit-style loaders; later chains used different infrastructure and backdoor components. The operation was targeted, with Kaspersky observing about a dozen machines across individuals and organizations.

Direct manual downloads from the official website were not the main path described here. The value was the updater trust boundary: a user asking Notepad++ to update could receive attacker code through infrastructure the project and its users expected to be boring.
